expansions.title: Data tables as a door
expansions.detail: If data tables is a use, the hit calls one interface. A door, a switch, and a pickup can share it without a new cast.

expansions.title: Data tables as data
expansions.detail: Designer numbers for data tables live on a row. AddToSlot through the interface when StackCount is positive, then the count is cleared reads the row instead of a literal.

expansions.title: Data tables as a listener
expansions.detail: Later systems listen for Begin Overlap. They do not incrementing the stack from the use trace, which would count a look as a pickup.

quiz.prompt: What is a data table for?
choices: A list of rows designers can edit without a code change.
A Tick function that designers comment out.
A replicated widget full of numbers.
The character's constructor, where every gun's stats are literals.
quiz.why: Rows, not code changes.
quiz.review_prompt: What is a data table for?

quiz.prompt: A new rifle needs a different magazine size. What should change?
choices: A row in the data table.
A new C++ branch for that rifle's name.
The HUD's hard-coded text.
The input action's default value.
quiz.why: Designers edit rows.
quiz.review_prompt: A new rifle needs a different magazine size. What should change?

quiz.prompt: True or false: A data table is a list of rows designers can edit without a code change.
choices: True
False
quiz.why: That is the lesson.
quiz.review_prompt: True or false: A data table is a list of rows designers can edit without a code change.

quiz.prompt: A weapon's magazine size can change in the data row without a programmer editing the reload function.
choices: True
False
quiz.why: The literals are what the table replaces.
quiz.review_prompt: True or false: Adding a weapon should require a programmer to edit the reload function's literals.

quiz.prompt: Who ships a balance change to magazine size after release?
choices: A designer, by editing the row. The reload code keeps reading that row.
A programmer, by recompiling a switch on the weapon name.
The player, by editing the widget at runtime as the source of truth.
The server RPC, whose argument is the new mag size from the client.
quiz.why: Code reads. Data changes.
quiz.review_prompt: Who ships a balance change to magazine size after release?

quiz.prompt: Two rows share one reload function. What stays in code?
choices: The rule: clamp Needed to the empty space and to the reserve. The numbers come from the row.
A copy of the function per row.
The mesh, compiled into the function.
A frame loop that scans the table for a row. The reload should read the row when the player asks.
quiz.why: One function, many rows.
quiz.review_prompt: Two rows share one reload function. What stays in code?

quiz.prompt: True or false: The same reload function can serve every firearm whose numbers live in the table.
choices: True
False
quiz.why: The function is the rule. The row is the numbers.
quiz.review_prompt: True or false: The same reload function can serve every firearm whose numbers live in the table.

quiz.prompt: A row is missing at runtime. What should the component do?
choices: Fail the lookup visibly and refuse to invent a magazine size.
Fall through to Tick and guess 30.
Use the widget's placeholder text as the mag size.
Replicate the entire table to every client as a mesh.
quiz.why: Missing data is an error, not a guess.
quiz.review_prompt: A row is missing at runtime. What should the component do?

quiz.prompt: True or false: Data tables are only for localization strings. Gameplay numbers belong in C++ literals.
choices: True
False
quiz.why: Gameplay numbers are the point of the table.
quiz.review_prompt: True or false: Data tables are only for localization strings. Gameplay numbers belong in C++ literals.

quiz.prompt: Where does a designer look to see every weapon's damage?
choices: The data table. Not a scatter of literals across components.
The character Tick.
The player controller input graph.
The health-change notify.
quiz.why: One list.
quiz.review_prompt: Where does a designer look to see every weapon's damage?

quiz.prompt: True or false: Changing a row still requires a new Blueprint cast in the reload graph.
choices: True
False
quiz.why: The cast list is what the row avoids.
quiz.review_prompt: True or false: Changing a row still requires a new Blueprint cast in the reload graph.

quiz.prompt: What does the player notice if two weapons share a row by mistake?
choices: They share magazine size, damage, or whatever else that row held, even though the meshes differ.
No row, if rows were only comments. Designers would be stuck editing C++ for every new gun.
The game will not cook.
Input unbinds the fire button.
quiz.why: The row is the identity of the numbers.
quiz.review_prompt: What does the player notice if two weapons share a row by mistake?

assignment.plainPrompt: Why is a data table a list of rows a designer can edit without a code change?
assignment.whyGamePrompt: What ships late if every balance tweak has to be a code change?

row.plainEnglish: The row struct is the shape.

expansions.title: Row struct as a door
expansions.detail: If row struct is a use, the hit calls one interface. A door, a switch, and a pickup can share it without a new cast.

expansions.title: Row struct as data
expansions.detail: Designer numbers for row struct live on a row. AddToSlot through the interface when StackCount is positive, then the count is cleared reads the row instead of a literal.

expansions.title: Row struct as a listener
expansions.detail: Later systems listen for Begin Overlap. They do not incrementing the stack from the use trace, which would count a look as a pickup.

quiz.prompt: What does a data table row inherit?
choices: FTableRowBase. That is the shape of one row.
An actor base, so the row could tick.
A widget base, so the row could draw itself.
The character class, so each row is a pawn.
quiz.why: The row struct is the shape.
quiz.review_prompt: What does a data table row inherit?

quiz.prompt: Magazine size, damage, and the mesh reference want to travel together. Where are they fields?
choices: On the row struct.
As three unrelated globals.
Inside a private text block on the bar.
As arguments on the server RPC the client fills in.
quiz.why: One struct, one row.
quiz.review_prompt: Magazine size, damage, and the mesh reference want to travel together. Where are they fields?

quiz.prompt: True or false: The row struct is the shape of one table row. It inherits FTableRowBase.
choices: True
False
quiz.why: That is the lesson.
quiz.review_prompt: True or false: The row struct is the shape of one table row. It inherits FTableRowBase.

quiz.prompt: True or false: A row struct should inherit AActor so designers can place rows in the level.
choices: True
False
quiz.why: A row is data, not a placed actor.
quiz.review_prompt: True or false: A row struct should inherit AActor so designers can place rows in the level.

quiz.prompt: Code asks the table for the rifle row. What does it get back?
choices: The struct: the fields the designer filled for that row.
A live actor already simulating in the world.
The widget that edits the table.
A random other row, because lookup is by index zero only.
quiz.why: Lookup returns the struct.
quiz.review_prompt: Code asks the table for the rifle row. What does it get back?

quiz.prompt: A field is added to the struct and not filled on old rows. What is the risk?
choices: Old weapons load a default for that field and behave as if the designer chose it.
No new field, if adding one deleted the row.
The table stops replicating.
Tick fills the field from the player's framerate.
quiz.why: Defaults are silent choices.
quiz.review_prompt: A field is added to the struct and not filled on old rows. What is the risk?

quiz.prompt: True or false: The component that reloads should read MagSize from the row struct instead of a literal 30.
choices: True
False
quiz.why: The struct holds the number.
quiz.review_prompt: True or false: The component that reloads should read MagSize from the row struct instead of a literal 30.

quiz.prompt: Who is allowed to treat the row as a pawn and call Tick on it?
choices: No one. It is not an actor.
The table, once per frame, so rows stay fresh.
The predicting machine, so it can simulate the row.
The replication callback, which would tick the struct when it arrives.
quiz.why: Rows do not tick.
quiz.review_prompt: Who is allowed to treat the row as a pawn and call Tick on it?

quiz.prompt: True or false: FTableRowBase means the struct is a networked character with authority.
choices: True
False
quiz.why: It means the struct can be a table row.
quiz.review_prompt: True or false: FTableRowBase means the struct is a networked character with authority.

quiz.prompt: Two tables need the same shape. Which type do both rows use?
choices: The row struct. Each table has its own rows.
One row, and the tables are views of that single struct instance.
The character class.
A Tick function.
quiz.why: Shape is the struct. Content is the rows.
quiz.review_prompt: Two tables need the same shape. What do they share?

quiz.prompt: True or false: Putting the mesh, the mag size, and the damage in different structs is clearer than one row.
choices: True
False
quiz.why: One row is the thing the designer edits.
quiz.review_prompt: True or false: Putting the mesh, the mag size, and the damage in different structs is clearer than one row.

quiz.prompt: What does a designer break by renaming a field without updating the code that reads it?
choices: The lookup still returns a row
No names, if field names were comments.
The input action rebinds.
Authority flips to the client.
quiz.why: The struct is a contract.
quiz.review_prompt: What does a designer break by renaming a field without updating the code that reads it?

assignment.plainPrompt: Why is the row struct the shape of one table row?
assignment.whyGamePrompt: What fails to load if two tables share a struct that matches neither row?

asset.whyGame: The actor points at the asset.

expansions.title: Data assets as a door
expansions.detail: If data assets is a use, the hit calls one interface. A door, a switch, and a pickup can share it without a new cast.

expansions.title: Data assets as data
expansions.detail: Designer numbers for data assets live on a row. Ammo increased by one, then the pickup actor destroys itself reads the row instead of a literal.

expansions.title: Data assets as a listener
expansions.detail: Later systems listen for Begin Overlap. They do not adding ammo from Tick, or leaving the pickup in the world after the count changes.

quiz.prompt: What is a primary data asset good for here?
choices: One item definition: an id, a mesh reference, and the rules. The pickup actor points at it.
A ticking actor that is the item.
A replicated widget for that item. The bar would then own the mesh and the rules.
The player's entire save game.
quiz.why: One asset, one item.
quiz.review_prompt: What is a primary data asset good for here?

quiz.prompt: Ten pickups in the level should share the medkit's rules. What do they point at?
choices: One data asset. They do not each embed a copy of the rules.
Ten copies of the rule code.
The heads-up display, which would store the medkit.
Each other, in a circle of actor references.
quiz.why: The actor points at the asset.
quiz.review_prompt: Ten pickups in the level should share the medkit's rules. What do they point at?

quiz.prompt: True or false: A data asset is one item definition: id, mesh reference, and rules. The pickup actor points at it.
choices: True
False
quiz.why: That is the lesson.
quiz.review_prompt: True or false: A data asset is one item definition: id, mesh reference, and rules. The pickup actor points at it.

quiz.prompt: True or false: The pickup actor should be the only place the mesh and the heal amount exist, with no asset.
choices: True
False
quiz.why: Then every pickup is a unique fork.
quiz.review_prompt: True or false: The pickup actor should be the only place the mesh and the heal amount exist, with no asset.

quiz.prompt: A designer changes the heal amount on the asset. What updates?
choices: Every pickup that points at that asset, without a code change.
Only pickups placed after the next compile, because the amount was copied into the actor.
The player controller's interact key.
OnRep of health, which reads the asset name as a float.
quiz.why: The asset is the shared definition.
quiz.review_prompt: A designer changes the heal amount on the asset. What updates?

quiz.prompt: What replicates when another player sees you holding the item?
choices: An id they can use to find the same asset. Not the asset object over the network as the inventory.
The data asset pointer, replicated as a live editor object. Clients need the values, not the editor asset.
The designer's uncommitted file.
The widget that edited the asset.
quiz.why: Replicate the id. Resolve the asset locally.
quiz.review_prompt: What replicates when another player sees you holding the item?

quiz.prompt: True or false: The pickup's Begin Overlap can read the heal amount from the asset it points at.
choices: True
False
quiz.why: The actor asks the asset.
quiz.review_prompt: True or false: The pickup's Begin Overlap can read the heal amount from the asset it points at.

quiz.prompt: Someone subclasses the pickup per item instead of pointing at assets. What grows?
choices: The class list, one Blueprint per item, with the rules copied.
No asset, if subclasses were the storage.
The row struct, which must inherit AActor.
A frame loop, if assets required one.
quiz.why: Assets avoid the class explosion.
quiz.review_prompt: Someone subclasses the pickup per item instead of pointing at assets. What grows?

quiz.prompt: True or false: A data asset should Tick so its rules stay updated.
choices: True
False
quiz.why: Assets are definitions. They do not simulate.
quiz.review_prompt: True or false: A data asset should Tick so its rules stay updated.

quiz.prompt: Where is the mesh reference stored so a pickup and a UI icon can share it?
choices: On the data asset both of them read.
Only on the pickup actor, with the UI casting to that actor in the level.
On the player controller.
Inside the server RPC argument the client types in.
quiz.why: One reference, two readers.
quiz.review_prompt: Where is the mesh reference stored so a pickup and a UI icon can share it?

quiz.prompt: True or false: Editing the asset while the game is running in a cooked build is the same as editing a C++ literal.
choices: True
False
quiz.why: The asset is data. A literal is code.
quiz.review_prompt: True or false: Editing the asset while the game is running in a cooked build is the same as editing a C++ literal.

quiz.prompt: What does the player see if a pickup's asset pointer is empty?
choices: No mesh and no heal amount, unless the actor invented defaults the designer did not choose.
A random other item, because empty means the first asset. An empty reference is a miss, not a wildcard.
The whole inventory UI, replicated.
Authority moves to that client.
quiz.why: Empty pointer, no definition.
quiz.review_prompt: What does the player see if a pickup's asset pointer is empty?

assignment.plainPrompt: Why does one data asset describe one item, with the actor pointing at that asset?
assignment.whyGamePrompt: What item do you spawn if the actor never points at an asset and a literal fills the gap?

reader.plainEnglish: The component reads. The widget draws.
reader.whyGame: The component that read the row owns the number.

expansions.title: Who reads the row as a door
expansions.detail: If who reads the row is a use, the hit calls one interface. A door, a switch, and a pickup can share it without a new cast.

expansions.title: Who reads the row as data
expansions.detail: Designer numbers for who reads the row live on a row. Needed clamped between zero and the empty space in the magazine, then added to Magazine and taken from Reserve reads the row instead of a literal.

expansions.title: Who reads the row as a listener
expansions.detail: Later systems listen for IA_Reload. They do not adding Needed inside Tick, or reloading when the mag is already full.

quiz.prompt: Who should read the weapon row?
choices: The weapon component. The widget does not decide magazine size.
The bar, because it is closer to the player's eyes.
The anim blueprint, which traces to discover the mag size.
The caller, stuffed into a server request argument.
quiz.why: The component reads. The widget draws.
quiz.review_prompt: Who should read the weapon row?

quiz.prompt: The HUD shows 30 rounds because that is what it drew last time. The row says 20. Who is wrong?
choices: The HUD, if it kept its own number instead of reading the component that read the row.
The row, because UI is the source of truth.
The input action.
The notify, which would copy the bar into the row. The bar is a view of the row, not the row's source.
quiz.why: The component that read the row owns the number.
quiz.review_prompt: The HUD shows 30 rounds because that is what it drew last time. The row says 20. Who is wrong?

quiz.prompt: True or false: The component reads the row. The widget does not decide magazine size.
choices: True
False
quiz.why: That is the lesson.
quiz.review_prompt: True or false: The component reads the row. The widget does not decide magazine size.

quiz.prompt: True or false: The widget should read the data table itself and ignore the component, so it can show a designer preview during play.
choices: True
False
quiz.why: Then the game and the UI can disagree.
quiz.review_prompt: True or false: The widget should read the data table itself and ignore the component, so it can show a designer preview during play.

quiz.prompt: Reload clamps Needed using MagSize. Where did MagSize come from?
choices: The component read it from the row when the weapon was equipped.
The widget typed it into a text box the component trusts.
Tick sampled the player's framerate.
A client RPC argument.
quiz.why: Read once from the row, use it in the rule.
quiz.review_prompt: Reload clamps Needed using MagSize. Where did MagSize come from?

quiz.prompt: A second system also reads the row and caches a different copy. What should it do instead?
choices: Ask the component that already read it, or read the same row and not keep a secret cache as authority.
Tick until the two caches match.
Replicate both caches and let clients vote. Two memories of one row will disagree the moment either side reloads.
Store the cache on the widget.
quiz.why: One reader the others ask.
quiz.review_prompt: A second system also reads the row and caches a different copy. What should it do instead?

quiz.prompt: True or false: The icon widget may read the display name from the same row the component uses for MagSize, and still must not write MagSize.
choices: True
False
quiz.why: Reading to display is fine. Deciding is not.
quiz.review_prompt: True or false: The icon widget may read the display name from the same row the component uses for MagSize, and still must not write MagSize.

quiz.prompt: Who runs the clamp?
choices: The component, with the numbers it read. Not the widget, and not the data asset's imaginary Tick.
The bar, inside its paint.
The row struct, which is an actor.
The local machine, before the server has the row. That copy becomes a second authority.
quiz.why: The component owns the rule.
quiz.review_prompt: Who runs the clamp?

quiz.prompt: True or false: If the widget and the component disagree, average them.
choices: True
False
quiz.why: Averaging hides the bug.
quiz.review_prompt: True or false: If the widget and the component disagree, average them.

quiz.prompt: A designer changes the row while you are in editor. What must be true on the next play?
choices: The component reads the new MagSize. The widget follows the component.
The widget keeps 30 until a programmer edits the paint.
Tick notices the file change and recompiles C++.
OnRep of an old save overwrites the row.
quiz.why: Readers pick up the row. They do not freeze a literal.
quiz.review_prompt: A designer changes the row while you are in editor. What must be true on the next play?

quiz.prompt: True or false: The anim blueprint should trace every frame to decide magazine size from whatever actor is in front of the camera.
choices: True
False
quiz.why: Magazine size is data, not a trace.
quiz.review_prompt: True or false: The anim blueprint should trace every frame to decide magazine size from whatever actor is in front of the camera.

quiz.prompt: What does the player notice when the widget decides magazine size and the component reloads from the row?
choices: The number on screen and the number that reloads are not the same number.
A faster reload, because two readers are quicker.
The data table deletes itself.
Input loses the fire button.
quiz.why: One reader decides.
quiz.review_prompt: What does the player notice when the widget decides magazine size and the component reloads from the row?

assignment.plainPrompt: Why does the component read the row, while the widget only draws?
assignment.whyGamePrompt: What number drifts if the widget reads the table itself and the component reads it again?
